questions.q: An import tariff in a labour surplus economy distributes income in favour of:
questions.exp: According to the Stolper-Samuelson theorem, an import tariff raises the real return to the owners of the relatively scarce factor (capital and specialized skills in a labor-surplus economy).

questions.q: International trade theory which provides that capital intensive country should export labour intensive goods and import capital goods is referred to as:
questions.exp: Wassily Leontief empirically found that the United States (a capital-abundant country) exported labor-intensive commodities, contradicting the Heckscher-Ohlin theorem, known as the Leontief Paradox.

questions.q:
The following table shows cost per unit of production of two goods, wheat and cloth in two countries X and Y with no transportation cost and free trade:
(i) Wheat -> Country X: 50 | Country Y: 350
(ii) Cloth -> Country X: 100 | Country Y: 500

Which one of the following will take place?
opts: X will export wheat and import cloth
X will export cloth and import wheat
There is no enough information to comment
questions.exp: Country X has comparative advantage in wheat (50/100 = 0.5 vs 350/500 = 0.7), and Country Y has comparative advantage in cloth. Thus, Country X will export wheat and import cloth.

questions.q:
Match the following List-I with List-II and select the correct answer:
A. Comparative Cost Theory of International Trade - (i) Gottfried Haberler
B. International Theory of Opportunity Cost - (ii) J.S. Mill
C. Factor Endowment Theory of International Trade - (iii) David Ricardo
D. Doctrine Of Reciprocal Demand - (iv) Heckscher-Ohlin

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Comparative Cost Theory was given by David Ricardo (iii), Opportunity Cost Theory by Gottfried Haberler (i), Factor Endowment by Heckscher-Ohlin (iv), and Reciprocal Demand by J.S. Mill (ii).

questions.q: In the two good Ricardian Trade Model, complete specialization in production occurs in free trade equilibrium because:
opts: The production possibility frontier satisfies increasing opportunity cost
There are diminishing returns to the factor of production
There are increasing returns to the factor of production
The production possibility frontier satisfies constant opportunity cost
questions.exp: The Ricardian trade model assumes constant returns to scale and constant labor costs, resulting in a linear production possibility frontier with constant opportunity costs.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
A. Supply side of international trade - (i) David Ricardo
B. Demand side of international trade - (ii) Bastable and Alfred Marshall
C. Opportunity cost international trade - (iii) G. Haberler
D. Real cost theory of international trade - (iv) Alfred Marshall and Edgeworth

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Supply side: David Ricardo (i); Demand side: Alfred Marshall & Edgeworth (iv); Opportunity cost: G. Haberler (iii); Real cost: Bastable & Alfred Marshall (ii).

questions.q: Where the foreign offer curve has an elasticity of one, the optimum tariff will be:
questions.exp: The formula for optimum tariff is t = 1 / (e - 1). When elasticity e = 1, the denominator is zero, making the optimum tariff infinity.

questions.q: If the sum of the elasticities of the exports and imports is less than one, any devaluation will further aggravate the deficit in the BOP. Who has given this view?
questions.exp: The Marshall-Lerner Condition states that currency devaluation improves the balance of payments only if the sum of price elasticities of demand for exports and imports is greater than 1.

questions.q: India is a net exporter of hand-made carpets and an importer of high-tech product like computer memory chips and printers. This pattern of India trade is explained by the:
questions.exp: The Heckscher-Ohlin Theory explains that a country will export goods that use its abundant factors of production (labor in India) and import goods that use scarce factors (capital/technology).

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of agreement between oligopolists? (December 2011)
questions.exp: OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is an international cartel formed by petroleum-producing nations operating in an oligopolistic market.

questions.q: Factor Endowment Theory of International Trade was propounded by:
questions.exp: The Factor Endowment Theory was formulated by Eli Heckscher and Bertil Ohlin.

questions.q: From the following modes of international business, identify the mode which involves strategic alliance:
questions.exp: A Joint Venture is a strategic alliance where two or more business entities pool resources and share risks to operate a separate entity.

questions.q: To ensure the validity of Heckscher-Ohlin theory of trade to be valid, the relative factor endowments of two countries should be:
questions.exp: The Heckscher-Ohlin theorem requires significant differences (divergence) in factor endowments between trading partners to generate comparative cost advantages.

questions.q:
Which of the following expressions amount to the import restriction measures?
(i) Currency control
(ii) Establishment of EPZs
(iii) Tariff cuts
(iv) Imposition of tariffs
(v) Imposition of non-tariff barriers

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Import restriction measures include foreign currency controls, tariffs, and non-tariff barriers.

questions.q: An MNC that maintains a balance between the home market and host market-oriented policies is:
questions.exp: In the EPRG framework, a Geocentric firm integrates both home and host nation perspectives into a balanced global approach.

questions.q: In international trade which of the following is a non-tariff trade barrier? (December 2014)
questions.exp: Anti-dumping regulations and procedural trade barriers act as administrative non-tariff barriers under trade agreements.

questions.q:
Match the items of List-I with items in List-II and select a correct code:
A. Current account - (i) Official capital
B. Capital account - (ii) Reserves from foreign countries
C. Unilateral payments - (iii) Reparations
D. Official statement account - (iv) Visible exports and imports

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Current account: Visible exports/imports (iv); Capital account: Official capital (i); Unilateral payments: Reparations (iii); Official settlement account: Foreign reserves (ii).

questions.q: When a company takes over another one and clearly becomes a new owner, the action is called (December 2010):
questions.exp: An acquisition occurs when one company takes over another and establishes clear ownership and control.

questions.q:
Match the items of List-I with the items in List-II and select the correct code (December 2014):
A. Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana - (i) Scheme intended to reduce difficulties of exporters
B. EPCG - (ii) Duty Entitlement Pass Book
C. DFRC - (iii) To boost exports of fruits, vegetables, flowers, minor forest produce, etc.
D. DEPB - (iv) Relating to import of duty-free fuel and capital goods

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana: Boost agri exports (iii); EPCG: Scheme to assist capital import difficulties (i); DFRC: Duty-free replenishment (iv); DEPB: Duty entitlement pass book (ii).

questions.q: What is not the advantage of SEZ? (September 2013)
opts: Improvement of infrastructure in the hinterland
Diversion of large tracts of farm land
questions.exp: Diversion of agricultural land for industrial setup is a disadvantage/criticism of SEZs.

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the assumptions of the Law of One Price? (September 2013)
(i) Restriction on the movement of goods between countries
(ii) No transportation costs
(iii) No tariffs

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: The Law of One Price assumes frictionless trade, meaning zero transportation costs and no tariffs or trade restrictions.

questions.q: The Ricardian theory of comparative advantages relates to:
questions.exp: The classical Ricardian model is static and analyzes short-run outcomes under constant technological conditions.

questions.q: The most important assumption in the Heckscher-Ohlin theory of international trade?
questions.exp: The standard Heckscher-Ohlin trade model assumes a 2x2x2 framework (two countries, two goods, two factors: labor and capital).

questions.q: Which of the following is not ensured to the consumer in the globalization?
opts: Clear origin of goods and services
questions.exp: Because global supply chains source components worldwide, clear single-country origin of goods is often obscured.

questions.q: All of the following are the features of globalization process except one. Which one is the exception?
opts: A reduction in artificial barrier to trade
A decline in the importance of international specialization
questions.exp: Globalization promotes the dismantling and reduction of trade barriers; increasing trade barriers is contrary to globalization.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The import volume tends to be very high when there is simultaneous high economic growth rate and a sharp fall in the relative price of imports and vice versa.
Reason (R): High rate of growth, ceteris paribus, is associated with rise in imports and increase in the imports, ceteris paribus, is associated with a fall in the relative price of imports.

Choose the correct code:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the right explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the right explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(R) is correct but (A) is not correct.
questions.exp: Higher national growth increases aggregate demand for imports, and lower relative import prices stimulate substitution toward foreign goods.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): An export processing zone is different from free trade zone as it promotes units primarily devoted to exports.
Reason (R): Goods imported to a free trade zone maybe re-exported without any processing, in the same form. But goods exported by units in an EPZ are expected to have undergone some value addition by manufacturing/processing.

Choose the correct code:
opts: (A) is correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.exp: FTZs serve commercial re-export and transshipment, while EPZs are specialized manufacturing units focused on value-added exports.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a favourable factor for globalization?
questions.exp: Technological obsolescence and resistance to modernization hinder globalization.

questions.q:
Match the items of List-I with items of List-II:
A. Measures towards globalization - (i) Off-shoring
B. Off-shoring - (ii) FEMA
C. FERA - (iii) Liberalise the inflow of FDI
D. Mr. Arthur Dunkel - (iv) Uruguay Round

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Measures towards globalization: FDI liberalization (iii); Off-shoring: Global services sourcing (i); FERA: Replaced by FEMA (ii); Arthur Dunkel: Uruguay Round (iv).

questions.q: Globalization is a term used to describe the process of removal of restrictions on which of the following?
questions.exp: Globalization represents the integration of national economies through free trade, investments, and mobility of factors of production.

questions.q:
According to Michael Porter, which of the following can be identified as four determinants of national competitive advantage?
(1) Factor Conditions
(2) Demand Conditions
(3) Firm Strategy, Structure, and Rivalry
(4) Related and Supporting Industries
(5) Financial Conditions
(6) Export Industry

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Michael Porter's Diamond model comprises: 1. Factor Conditions, 2. Demand Conditions, 3. Firm Strategy, Structure & Rivalry, and 4. Related & Supporting Industries.

questions.q: Under communism, which of the following persons gave the surplus value theory of wage?
questions.exp: Karl Marx formulated the surplus value theory of wages, explaining the extraction of surplus labor under capitalism.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a benefit of privatization?
questions.exp: Concentration of economic power in private monopolies is a risk and disadvantage of unregulated privatization.

questions.q:
Which of the following are the main benefits of international trade?
(1) Specialization benefits world trade as it enables different nations with differing skills and resources to gain the rewards from the division of labour.
(2) There is potential gain of economies of scale when there is good size of market.
(3) Competition is fostered by free trade.
(4) Lower prices are greater choices to consumers.

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: International trade expands production efficiency through specialization, scale economies, competition, and lower consumer prices.

questions.q:
Which of the following assumptions are true in context of theory of comparative advantage?
(1) Two trading economies each producing the same two goods.
(2) The factors of production in each economy are perfectly mobile.
(3) There are no trade barriers and no transport costs.
(4) The state of technology is unchanged.

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: The Ricardian model assumes factors are perfectly mobile internally but immobile internationally, along with 2 goods, zero transport costs, and constant technology.

questions.q: International trade is theoretically based on which principle?
questions.exp: The Theory of Comparative Advantage is the fundamental basis demonstrating mutual trade gains even without absolute cost advantages.

questions.q: A country is said to have a comparative advantage in the production of a good when:
opts: it can produce more of it than any other country.
it has captured a larger share of the world market than any other country.
it can produce it at a lower opportunity cost than its trading partners.
its costs of production tor the good are lower than in other countries.
questions.exp: Comparative advantage is defined by the ability to produce a good at a lower relative opportunity cost.

questions.q: The existence of international trade is best explained by the fact that countries:
opts: Operate with their own unique currencies, impacting trade values and exchanges.
Implement varied economic systems, from free markets to centrally planned economies, influencing their trade policies and practices.
Possess varying endowments of natural resources, labor, and capital, leading to differences in production capabilities and costs.
Specialize in the production of certain goods and services based on their comparative advantages, enhancing global trade efficiency.
questions.exp: Disparities in factor endowments (natural resources, labor, capital) lead to differing cost advantages that drive international trade.

questions.q: What could lead to a decline in a country's exports?
opts: A depreciation of the country's currency, making its exports cheaper abroad.
A decrease in tariff barriers by other countries, making it easier to export goods to those countries.
A reduction in the marginal propensity to import among trading partners, indicating they are less inclined to buy foreign goods.
An increase in the country's imports, which affects its trade balance but not directly its exports.
questions.exp: A lower marginal propensity to import in foreign partner nations directly reduces their demand for imported goods.

questions.q: Which of the following is not typically considered a component of a company's internal environment?
opts: The values held by the company's shareholders.
questions.exp: Customers are part of the external operating/micro environment, not the internal organization.

questions.q: Keeping in the process of globalization, 'Levitt Thesis' means:
opts: There should be standardization strategy for products and aggressive low pricing.
There is homogenization of the same products throughout the world.
There should be customized products to meet the national market.
questions.exp: Theodore Levitt argued that global technology and communication create homogenized consumer demand across world markets.

questions.q: The companies globalize their operations through different means:
questions.exp: Firms globalize through trade (exporting), contractual transfers (licensing/franchising), and investment modes (JVs/FDI).

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)?
opts: It enables executives to concentrate on strategy.
It improves process and saves money.
questions.exp: BPO enhances an enterprise's organizational efficiency by transferring transactional operations to specialized vendors.

questions.q: Who among the following has given Absolute Advantage Model of International trade?
questions.exp: Adam Smith propounded the Theory of Absolute Advantage in 1776.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Indian companies have established subsidiaries and joint ventures in a number of countries in different manufacturing industries and service sectors.
Reason (R): By restricting the areas of operations and growth, the government policy seriously constrained the potential of Indian companies to make a foray into the foreign countries.

Choose the correct code:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the right explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the right explanation of (A).
questions.exp: Both statements are historically true, but past policy constraints do not explain the post-1991 expansion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Served From India Scheme (SFIS) has been replaced with Service Exports from India Scheme (SEIS).
Statement II: The rate of reward under SEIS would be based on net foreign exchange earned.

Choose the correct code:
opts: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement II is correct, but statement I is incorrect.
Both the statements I and II are incorrect.
Both the statements I and II are correct.
questions.exp: Under FTP 2015-20, SFIS was replaced by SEIS, providing duty credit scrips on net foreign exchange earnings.

questions.q:
Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2015-2020, which of the following additional ports are allowed for export and import?
(A) Calicut Airport, Kerala
(B) Rajkot Airport, Gujarat
(C) Arakonam ICD, Tamil Nadu
(D) Ludhiana Airport, Punjab

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Calicut Airport and Arakkonam ICD were designated as cargo clearance ports under FTP 2015-20.

questions.q:
Examine the following statements and choose the correct code:
Statement I: Companies with Low cash reserves normally prefer Licensing mode rather than Foreign Direct Investment.
Statement II: Cash rich firms normally prefer Foreign Direct Investment.

Choose the correct code:
opts: (I) is not correct but (II) is correct
questions.exp: Licensing requires minimal financial capital outlay, whereas FDI requires high resource commitment.

questions.q: What does counter-trade refer to?
opts: A trade mechanism where goods are exchanged directly for other goods without using a conventional monetary transaction, involving a seller providing goods to a buyer in exchange for a different set of goods.
A trading strategy where a country limits its imports to those countries that buy its exports.
A financial strategy where trades are executed to take advantage of price differences in two or more markets.
A method of international trade where transactions are carried out using a single currency for simplification.
questions.exp: Counter-trade is an exchange of goods and services where non-cash barter or reciprocal purchase agreements replace hard currency settlement.

questions.q: Globalization is the term used to describe process of removal of restriction on which of the following?
questions.exp: Globalization removes cross-border barriers on trade in goods and services as well as investment capital.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an issue for which an agreement has not been made between two or more countries?
opts: Deep-sea mining in non-coastal areas of the oceans
Banning the use of certain pesticides
questions.exp: Regulatory jurisdiction over deep-sea mining in international non-coastal seabed waters remains unresolved.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of bartering internationally?
opts: Bartering is a type of service export and import.
questions.exp: Barter primarily involves physical commodity exchange rather than intangible services.

questions.q:
Match the items of List-I with items of List-II:
A. Wider Market - (i) Modes of Entry
B. Turn-key Projects - (ii) Goal of International Business
C. Expanding the production capacities - (iii) Advantages of International Business
D. Geocentric approach - (iv) Stage of Globalization

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Wider market: Advantage (iii); Turnkey: Entry mode (i); Capacity expansion: Goal (ii); Geocentric: Globalization stage (iv).

questions.q: The method being used for Transferring Complex Technology is known as:
questions.exp: Turnkey contracts encompass engineering, construction, and commissioning for complex industrial technology transfers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): International business has grown in more recent years at a faster pace than global production.
Reason (R): Growth through trade has increased, but growth through foreign direct investment has not.

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Trade growth outpaced output, but global FDI has also expanded substantially (making Reason R false).

questions.q: Which one of the following is not the benefit of MNCs to the host nation?
questions.exp: Displacement of local traditional businesses and cultural friction are recognized negative consequences of MNC operations.

questions.q: Why is a project in international business referred to as a "turnkey project"?
opts: It involves the licensee constructing a complete facility in their own country before transferring ownership.
It signifies a project where the contractor (licensor) fully completes the project to the point of operation before handing it over to the project owner (licensee), ready for immediate use.
It describes a scenario where the contractor (licensor) initiates the project, then invites the project owner (licensee) to finish the remaining work.
It pertains to a project undertaken collaboratively by the contractor (licensor) and the project owner (licensee), with profits shared equally upon completion.
questions.exp: In a turnkey project, the developer builds the plant completely and delivers the finished operating project to the client.

questions.q: EPCG denotes:
questions.exp: EPCG stands for Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme for concessional capital imports against export obligations.

questions.q: India suffered from deficit balance both in trade balance and net invisibles, hence, took up a number of steps to manage this problem. Which one is not appropriate for this?
questions.exp: Export control restricts trade earnings and worsens balance of payments deficits.

questions.q:
Match the following books with their authors:
A. India and Economic Reforms - (i) Bhagwati, J.
B. Development Planning: The Indian Experience - (ii) Chakravarty, S.
C. India: Economic Development and Social Opportunity - (iii) Jean Dreze and Amartya Sen
D. Fiscal Policy of Underdeveloped Countries - (iv) Chelliah, R.J.

Choose the correct code:
questions.exp: Bhagwati: Economic Reforms; Chakravarty: Development Planning; Dreze & Sen: Development and Social Opportunity; Chelliah: Fiscal Policy.

questions.q: Special Economic Zones (SEZ) have been created first time in the:
questions.exp: The SEZ policy was officially introduced in the EXIM Policy of April 2000.

questions.q: DFEC stands for:
questions.exp: DFEC stands for Duty Free Export Credit scheme.
